hints: Differentiate velocity $v = 4.5 + 4t - 0.5t^2$ with respect to $t$ to find acceleration $a(t)$.
Substitute this value of $t$ back into the velocity formula.
walkthrough:
State the foundational relationship between acceleration and velocity:
$$a = \frac{dv}{dt}$$

Differentiate the given velocity function $v(t) = 4.5 + 4t - 0.5t^2$ term by term:
$$\frac{d}{dt}(4.5) = 0$$
$$\frac{d}{dt}(4t) = 4$$
$$\frac{d}{dt}(-0.5t^2) = -0.5(2t) = -t$$
$$a(t) = 4 - t$$

Find when acceleration is zero by setting $a(t) = 0$:
$$4 - t = 0 \implies t = 4\text{ s}$$

hints: Find the time when the particle arrives at $Q$ by setting $v = 0$: $4.5 + 4t - 0.5t^2 = 0$.
Multiply by 2 and solve the quadratic $t^2 - 8t - 9 = 0$ to get $t = 9\text{ s}$.
Integrate the velocity function from $t = 0$ to $t = 9$ to find the distance $PQ$.
walkthrough:
Determine the time of arrival at point $Q$. The particle comes to rest at $Q$, so set $v(t) = 0$:
$$4.5 + 4t - 0.5t^2 = 0$$
Multiply the entire equation by $-2$ to obtain a monic quadratic with integer coefficients:
$$t^2 - 8t - 9 = 0$$
Factorize the quadratic expression:
$$(t - 9)(t + 1) = 0$$
Since time must be non-negative ($t \ge 0$), discard $t = -1$:
$$t = 9\text{ s}$$

State the relationship between displacement and velocity:
$$s = \int_0^9 v(t)\,dt$$
Substitute the velocity expression:
$$s = \int_0^9 (4.5 + 4t - 0.5t^2)\,dt$$

Integrate term by term using the power rule:
$$\int 4.5\,dt = 4.5t$$
$$\int 4t\,dt = 2t^2$$
$$\int -0.5t^2\,dt = -\frac{0.5t^3}{3} = -\frac{t^3}{6}$$
$$s = \left[4.5t + 2t^2 - \frac{t^3}{6}\right]_0^9$$
